correctness.rationale: The three distinct proper positive divisors of an odd instance are odd, so sigma(n) is odd and every prime exponent is even. For n=p²q²r², bound the sum of d_i/n by taking the reciprocals of the three smallest distinct divisors greater than one. The ordered denominators are bounded below respectively by (7,11,13) when p≥7, by (5,7,13) when p=5 and r≥13, and by (3,9,37) when p=3 and q≥37. Exact rational substitution gives all three strict exclusions. The remaining q-list for p=3 is exhaustive and every signature selection gives a genuine polynomial identity A r²−B r−C=0 with B,C>0. An independent exact enumeration found the positive integral roots by checking the divisors of C, since r must divide C. It reproduced 23,400 selections, 22,620 positive leading coefficients, 57 square discriminants and all nine integral roots r>q; precisely four roots counted with signature multiplicity are prime. Trial-divisor enumeration also gives exactly the two triples for 27225 and one each for 38025 and 53361, and no triple of sum 61,439 for the sole residual case 148225. This is an all-prime classification because the reduction to finitely many polynomials did not bound r empirically. The multiplicity-six equivalent formulation is restricted to odd exactly 3-deficient-perfect integers with three distinct prime factors.

value.rationale: The exponent layer is forced as the first eligible odd layer after the known two-prime result, not selected by an arbitrary numerical cutoff. The classification bounds an unbounded third-prime search and determines actual witness multiplicities, including a number with two distinct triples, useful when organizing the broader three-prime case. It does not resolve the larger even exponents.
